name: the detail-page card ignores the Ctrl gate on hover
why: By default (sa_dp_hover_without_ctrl off) only a hover with Ctrl held may schedule the card. Without the gate a pointer crossing the table pops cards and fetches pages again. Since the popup engine (org/iframe.org Phase 1) this is the engine's one gate line, asked of each source (t.src.needsCtrl()).
grep: by default a plain hover shows nothing

name: pressing Ctrl on a hovered title does nothing
why: Ctrl pressed while the pointer already rests on a title must show its card at once; without the keydown branch only a hover that STARTS with Ctrl held would.
grep: Ctrl pressed while the pointer rests on a title

name: the plain-hover setting is ignored
why: sa_dp_hover_without_ctrl: true restores the old behaviour; read wrongly, a plain hover would stay silent with the setting on.
grep: with the setting on, a plain hover shows the card

name: the "#" card ignores the Ctrl gate on hover
why: By default (sa_event_rg_tooltip_without_ctrl off) entering a "#" cell without Ctrl must neither show the card nor start a lookup. Since the popup engine the gate is the "#" source's needsCtrl().
grep: a plain hover shows no card and asks nothing

name: a plain hover keeps the card an earlier Ctrl press left
why: The guard this entry first planted (the stale data-mbtt a Ctrl press left on the cell) is gone with its mechanism: the popup engine keeps no card state on the cell. The same test's nearest guard is the engine's: leaving the cell hides the card, so a later plain hover finds none showing.
grep: Ctrl pressed while the pointer is on a

name: pressing Ctrl on a "#" cell shows nothing
why: Ctrl pressed while the pointer rests on a "#" cell must show its card at once. Since the popup engine that is the engine's keydown branch (_dpCtrlTarget()), the same line the detail-page entry above plants, seen here by the "#" spec.
grep: Ctrl pressed while the pointer is on a

name: the "#" plain-hover setting is ignored
why: sa_event_rg_tooltip_without_ctrl: true restores the old plain hover.

name: a chip replaces the selection instead of toggling it
why: The pre-multi-select behaviour: a second chip would REPLACE the first, so Front then Medium would show only Medium.

edits.find: const next = !type ? [] : sel.includes(type) ? sel.filter(t => t !== type) : [...sel, type];

name: the union duplicates an image carrying two selected types
why: Image 2 is Back + Front; a union built per type (concat) would show it twice when both chips are pressed.

edits.replace:
(images[i].types && images[i].types.length ? images[i].types : ['(no type)']).some(t => want.has(t)))
            .flatMap(i => (images[i].types || []).filter(t => want.has(t)).map(() => i).slice(0, want.size ? undefined : 1));

name: the All chip stays pressed beside selected types
why: aria-pressed on All must mean 'nothing selected'; pressed always, it would claim All while a type filters.

name: the viewer ignores the multi-chip selection in Spreads
why: _releaseArtViewerOrder() must read the same selection as the render; reading none, the Spreads viewer would step through every image.
